lines.raw: Think about a family in a village where the nearest health post is a three-hour walk, the water source is not safe, and money from a son working abroad arrives only now and then.
lines.say: Think about a family in a village where the nearest health post is a three-hour walk, the water source is not safe, and money from a son working abroad arrives only now and then.

lines.raw: Even with the best doctor in the world, this family will find it hard to stay healthy.
lines.say: Even with the best doctor in the world, this family will find it hard to stay healthy.

scenes.section: Health is made mostly outside the hospital

lines.raw: The conditions in which people are born, live, work and grow old are called the **social determinants of health**, or **SDOH**.
lines.say: The conditions in which people are born, live, work and grow old are called the social determinants of health, or S D O H.

lines.raw: Researchers often estimate that medical care explains only a minority of a population's health; much of the rest comes from behaviour, environment and social and economic conditions.
lines.say: Researchers often estimate that medical care explains only a minority of a population's health; much of the rest comes from behaviour, environment and social and economic conditions.

scenes.section: Health is made mostly outside the hospital

lines.raw: Familiar examples from Nepal.
lines.say: Familiar examples from Nepal.

lines.raw: Children in homes without clean water get diarrhoea more often.
lines.say: Children in homes without clean water get diarrhoea more often.

lines.raw: Kathmandu's winter air pollution makes asthma and cough worse.
lines.say: Kathmandu's winter air pollution makes asthma and cough worse.

lines.raw: An elderly person living alone in a hill village may skip medicine because nobody can fetch it from the bazaar.
lines.say: An elderly person living alone in a hill village may skip medicine because nobody can fetch it from the bazaar.

lines.raw: None of these problems is solved by a prescription alone.
lines.say: None of these problems is solved by a prescription alone.

scenes.section: Health is made mostly outside the hospital

lines.raw: Five areas of SDOH, as grouped by the US government's Healthy People 2030 framework.
lines.say: Five areas of S D O H, as grouped by the U S government's Healthy People 2030 framework.

lines.raw: **Economic stability**. Examples of a need: Low income, job loss, debt, not enough food. How it affects health: Skipping medicine or meals to pay rent.
lines.say: Economic stability. Examples of a need: Low income, job loss, debt, not enough food. How it affects health: Skipping medicine or meals to pay rent.

lines.raw: **Education access and quality**. Examples of a need: Low reading level. How it affects health: Cannot follow written medicine instructions.
lines.say: Education access and quality. Examples of a need: Low reading level. How it affects health: Cannot follow written medicine instructions.

lines.raw: **Health care access and quality**. Examples of a need: No nearby clinic, no insurance, language barriers. How it affects health: Problems found late, when they are harder to treat.
lines.say: Health care access and quality. Examples of a need: No nearby clinic, no insurance, language barriers. How it affects health: Problems found late, when they are harder to treat.

lines.raw: **Neighborhood and built environment**. Examples of a need: No transport, unsafe housing, pollution. How it affects health: Missed appointments; asthma triggered at home.
lines.say: Neighborhood and built environment. Examples of a need: No transport, unsafe housing, pollution. How it affects health: Missed appointments; asthma triggered at home.

lines.raw: **Social and community context**. Examples of a need: Living alone, isolation, discrimination. How it affects health: Nobody notices when someone gets worse.
lines.say: Social and community context. Examples of a need: Living alone, isolation, discrimination. How it affects health: Nobody notices when someone gets worse.

lines.raw: Recording social needs: Z-codes.
lines.say: Recording social needs: Z-codes.

lines.raw: Diagnoses on claims are recorded as **ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes** (covered in the Medical course), like `E11.9` for type 2 diabetes.
lines.say: Diagnoses on claims are recorded as I C D 10-CM diagnosis codes (covered in the Medical course), like E 1 1 . 9 for type 2 diabetes.

lines.raw: ICD-10-CM also has codes for social problems.
lines.say: I C D 10-CM also has codes for social problems.

lines.raw: They start with **Z**, and the group from **`Z55` to `Z65`** is used for social and economic circumstances.
lines.say: They start with Z, and the group from Z55 to Z65 is used for social and economic circumstances.

lines.raw: They are called **Z-codes** or **SDOH Z-codes**.
lines.say: They are called Z-codes or S D O H Z-codes.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: `Z56.0`. Meaning: Unemployment, unspecified. Example: Daniel lost his job in mid-2025 (in this story his doctor recorded it at an August check-up).
lines.say: Z 5 6 . 0. Meaning: Unemployment, unspecified. Example: Daniel lost his job in mid-2025 (in this story his doctor recorded it at an August check-up).

lines.raw: `Z59.41`. Meaning: Food insecurity. Example: A member says they often run out of food before the end of the month.
lines.say: Z 5 9 . 4 1. Meaning: Food insecurity. Example: A member says they often run out of food before the end of the month.

lines.raw: `Z59.6`. Meaning: Low income. Example: A member cannot afford their medicines.
lines.say: Z 5 9 . 6. Meaning: Low income. Example: A member cannot afford their medicines.

lines.raw: `Z59.82`. Meaning: Transportation insecurity. Example: A member has no car and no bus route to the clinic.
lines.say: Z 5 9 . 8 2. Meaning: Transportation insecurity. Example: A member has no car and no bus route to the clinic.

lines.raw: `Z59.00`. Meaning: Homelessness, unspecified. Example: A member has no stable place to live.
lines.say: Z 5 9 . 0 0. Meaning: Homelessness, unspecified. Example: A member has no stable place to live.

lines.raw: `Z60.2`. Meaning: Problems related to living alone. Example: An elderly member lives alone with nobody to check on them.
lines.say: Z 6 0 . 2. Meaning: Problems related to living alone. Example: An elderly member lives alone with nobody to check on them.

lines.raw: Reading a Z-code.
lines.say: Reading a Z-code.

lines.raw: Z: Chapter for factors that affect health status or contact with health services (not a disease itself).
lines.say: Z: Chapter for factors that affect health status or contact with health services (not a disease itself).

lines.raw: 59: Problems related to housing and economic circumstances.
lines.say: 59: Problems related to housing and economic circumstances.

lines.raw: .82: Transportation insecurity, the specific problem.
lines.say: .82: Transportation insecurity, the specific problem.

lines.raw: Z-codes are under-used.
lines.say: Z-codes are under-used.

lines.raw: Z-codes appear on only a small share of claims, because doctors are busy and social needs are not always asked about.
lines.say: Z-codes appear on only a small share of claims, because doctors are busy and social needs are not always asked about.

lines.raw: So **no Z-code does not mean no need**.
lines.say: So no Z-code does not mean no need.

lines.raw: Teams also use short **screening questionnaires** (for example, the Accountable Health Communities screening tool from CMS, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services) and outside data, like neighbourhood income, to fill the gap.
lines.say: Teams also use short screening questionnaires (for example, the Accountable Health Communities screening tool from C M S, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services) and outside data, like neighbourhood income, to fill the gap.

lines.raw: In the US: What a health plan can do about social needs.
lines.say: In the U S: What a health plan can do about social needs.

lines.raw: Connect members to **food banks** and government food help.
lines.say: Connect members to food banks and government food help.

lines.raw: Arrange **rides** to appointments (some Medicaid and Medicare Advantage plans offer this).
lines.say: Arrange rides to appointments (some Medicaid and Medicare Advantage plans offer this).

lines.raw: Send **90-day mail-order** prescriptions so members do not need to travel to a pharmacy every month.
lines.say: Send 90-day mail-order prescriptions so members do not need to travel to a pharmacy every month.

lines.raw: Ask a **community health worker** to visit.
lines.say: Ask a community health worker to visit.

lines.raw: This US role is very similar to an FCHV: a trusted local person who helps neighbours reach care.
lines.say: This U S role is very similar to an F C H V: a trusted local person who helps neighbours reach care.

lines.raw: Prevention and screening.
lines.say: Prevention and screening.

lines.raw: The cheapest illness is the one that never happens, and the second cheapest is the one caught early.
lines.say: The cheapest illness is the one that never happens, and the second cheapest is the one caught early.

lines.raw: **Prevention** includes vaccines, healthy habits and **screening**: testing people who feel fine to find problems early.
lines.say: Prevention includes vaccines, healthy habits and screening: testing people who feel fine to find problems early.

lines.raw: Common US preventive services (based on national recommendations; details depend on age, sex and risk).

lines.raw: **Well-child visits and childhood vaccines**. Who it is for: Babies and children, on a set schedule. In our story: Lily (6) has a yearly well-child visit.
lines.say: Well-child visits and childhood vaccines. Who it is for: Babies and children, on a set schedule. In our story: Lily (6) has a yearly well-child visit.

lines.raw: **Yearly flu vaccine**. Who it is for: Almost everyone aged 6 months and over. In our story: The whole Carter family.
lines.say: Yearly flu vaccine. Who it is for: Almost everyone aged 6 months and over. In our story: The whole Carter family.

lines.raw: **Blood pressure check**. Who it is for: All adults. In our story: Emily and Daniel at their check-ups.
lines.say: Blood pressure check. Who it is for: All adults. In our story: Emily and Daniel at their check-ups.

lines.raw: **Cholesterol and diabetes screening**. Who it is for: Adults in certain age ranges or with risk factors. In our story: Emily's cholesterol was found this way.
lines.say: Cholesterol and diabetes screening. Who it is for: Adults in certain age ranges or with risk factors. In our story: Emily's cholesterol was found this way.

lines.raw: **Colorectal (bowel) cancer screening**. Who it is for: Adults aged 45 to 75. In our story: Robert (68).
lines.say: Colorectal (bowel) cancer screening. Who it is for: Adults aged 45 to 75. In our story: Robert (68).

lines.raw: **Mammogram** (breast cancer screening). Who it is for: Women aged 40 to 74, every 2 years. In our story: Emily, from age 40.
lines.say: Mammogram (breast cancer screening). Who it is for: Women aged 40 to 74, every 2 years. In our story: Emily, from age 40.

lines.raw: **Annual Wellness Visit**. Who it is for: People with Medicare. In our story: Robert, once a year.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: Social determinants of health (food, money, transport, housing, isolation) shape health a great deal, often more than medical care alone.
lines.say: Social determinants of health (food, money, transport, housing, isolation) shape health a great deal, often more than medical care alone.
